Call Fabric functions as the signed-in user

Source: R/backend__fabric.R
oauth_db_fabric_api.Rd

Use Fabric services with each visitor's Microsoft account. Pass a fabricQueryR function to $call() to list workspaces, query semantic models or read OneLake data. The client supplies the user's credentials and returns the function's result.

Usage

oauth_db_fabric_api(
  authorization,
  targets = list(fabric = "fabric", sql = "sql", dax = "power_bi", kql = "kusto", onelake
    = "storage", graphql = "power_bi"),
  required_scopes = list(),
  min_valid_for = 60,
  session = shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain()
)

Arguments

authorization

Function providing the visitor's current sign-in authorization. Pass auth$connection from shinyOAuth without parentheses. To select a saved account, use a function calling auth$connection(id).

targets

Named vector or list mapping services to shinyOAuth token targets. Defaults match oauth_db_microsoft_client(). A supplied mapping replaces the defaults. Use list(kql = NULL) for one service without a named target.

required_scopes

Named list of additional permissions to check, by service. Set client and target requirements in shinyOAuth.

min_valid_for

Minimum remaining token lifetime, in seconds, when obtaining a token. Use 0 to accept any unexpired token.

session

The visitor's Shiny session. Usually inferred when you create the helper inside server().

Value

A client object with these methods:

  • $call(.fn, ...) calls a fabricQueryR function and returns its result, including resource objects. Omit token from the function arguments.

  • $token_provider() returns a token callback for calling a fabricQueryR function directly.

Details

Create the client inside server() and call its methods from render or reactive expressions. Configure oauth_db_microsoft_client() for the services your app needs first. Users need access to the Fabric items and data they query.

Resource objects

A fabricQueryR object, such as a Lakehouse, keeps the authorization used to create it. Put the lookup inside reactive() so it runs again when the visitor changes accounts, as in the example.

For a DBI connection managed by shinyOAuthDB, use oauth_db_fabric_sql(). Your app must close connections it opens through fabricQueryR functions or object methods.

Custom token targets

The targets mapping selects the service tokens this client can use. DAX and GraphQL share the Power BI resource and must use the same target; different resources need different targets. Tokens are obtained when a service needs them.

See also

oauth_db_microsoft_client(), oauth_db_fabric_sql(). vignette("fabric", package = "shinyOAuthDB") has sign-in setup and a complete app.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Microsoft client configured with services = c("fabric", "onelake"):
fabric <- oauth_db_fabric_api(auth$connection)
lakehouse <- shiny::reactive({
  fabric$call(
    fabricQueryR::fabric_item,
    workspace = "workspace-guid",
    item = "lakehouse-guid"
  )
})
output$rows <- shiny::renderTable({
  lakehouse()$read_table("Orders", limit = 100L)
})
} # }
